source.title: Source definitions and tests
source.description: Synthetic partner, title, review and publication sources with key and relationship tests.
source.code:
version: 2

sources:
  - name: partner_platform
    description: Synthetic partner publishing inputs seeded for this portfolio reference.
    schema: main
    tables:
      - name: raw_partners
        description: One current row per synthetic partner. Partner name, region and current tier depend on partner_id rather than being copied into title or event rows.
        columns:
          - name: partner_id
            data_tests: [unique, not_null]
      - name: raw_titles
        description: One current row per synthetic title. partner_id is a foreign key; partner attributes stay in raw_partners.
        columns:
          - name: title_id
            data_tests: [unique, not_null]
          - name: partner_id
            data_tests:
              - not_null
              - relationships:
                  arguments:
                    to: source('partner_platform', 'raw_partners')
                    field: partner_id
      - name: raw_submissions
        description: One row per review attempt; status and build version depend on submission_id, while title attributes stay in raw_titles.
        columns:
          - name: submission_id
            data_tests: [unique, not_null]
          - name: title_id
            data_tests:
              - not_null
              - relationships:
                  arguments:
                    to: source('partner_platform', 'raw_titles')
                    field: title_id
      - name: raw_publications
        description: One storefront publication event per row. Storefront region depends on publication_id; title and partner attributes are referenced by key.
        columns:
          - name: publication_id
            data_tests: [unique, not_null]
          - name: title_id
            data_tests:
              - not_null
              - relationships:
                  arguments:
                    to: source('partner_platform', 'raw_titles')
                    field: title_id

normalization.title: 3NF to dimensional handoff
normalization.description: Functional dependencies, source keys, foreign keys and the move to title-grain and dimensional analytics.
normalization.code:
# The 3NF boundary in the synthetic publishing reference

The four seeded source tables separate four business entities. Each has one declared key. Attributes describe that key, not another non-key attribute in the same row.

| Relation | Primary key | Functional dependency in this fixture | Reference |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Partner | `partner_id` | `partner_id → partner_name, region, partner_tier` | — |
| Title | `title_id` | `title_id → partner_id, title_name, platform, planned_release_at` | `partner_id → Partner` |
| Submission | `submission_id` | `submission_id → title_id, submitted_at, reviewed_at, status, build_version` | `title_id → Title` |
| Publication | `publication_id` | `publication_id → title_id, published_at, storefront_region` | `title_id → Title` |

For this fixture, a title has one partner and one platform. If a production title can have several platforms or release plans, that relationship needs its own keyed table; copying a list into `raw_titles` would break this design.

The practical 3NF rule is that non-key attributes depend on the key, the whole key, and no other non-key attribute. Partner region lives with Partner, not repeated on Title or Submission. Review status lives with a Submission, while a storefront region lives with a Publication. Changing a partner name therefore needs one source-row update, rather than a repair across every title and event.

The source contract in [`models/staging/sources.yml`](../models/staging/sources.yml) checks primary-key uniqueness and non-nullness, plus foreign-key relationships. Those tests protect the declared keys; they do not prove every real-world functional dependency. The partner-tier [`snapshot`](../snapshots/partner_tier_history.sql) handles change over time separately. Its as-of model leaves events before the first captured version unknown.

The analytics layer deliberately changes shape. [`int_title_outcomes`](../models/intermediate/int_title_outcomes.sql) aggregates review and publication streams separately before joining at title grain. [`fct_submission`](../models/marts/fct_submission.sql) keeps attempt grain; [`dim_partner`](../models/marts/dim_partner.sql) offers a readable dimension. The [`partner mart`](../models/marts/mart_partner_publishing.sql) then answers questions without forcing every dashboard to rejoin the normalized event tables. This is a modeled handoff from a 3NF-shaped source to a dimensional analytics product, not a claim that the final mart is in 3NF.

stage.title: Typed staging model
stage.description: One named place to cast times and standardise review status.
stage.code:
select
    cast(submission_id as varchar) as submission_id,
    cast(title_id as varchar) as title_id,
    cast(submitted_at as timestamp) as submitted_at,
    cast(reviewed_at as timestamp) as reviewed_at,
    lower(trim(status)) as status,
    cast(build_version as integer) as build_version
from {{ source('partner_platform', 'raw_submissions') }}

snapshot.title: Partner tier snapshot
snapshot.description: Timestamp strategy preserves partner-tier changes as history.

asof.title: Tier at submission
asof.description: An as-of join leaves pre-capture history unknown rather than using a future tier.
asof.code:
-- A snapshot begins at its first captured version. Do not fill earlier events with today's tier.
select
    s.submission_id,
    s.partner_id,
    s.submitted_at,
    h.partner_tier as tier_at_submission,
    h.dbt_valid_from as tier_valid_from,
    h.dbt_valid_to as tier_valid_to,
    case when h.partner_id is null then 0 else 1 end as tier_history_available
from {{ ref('int_submission_lifecycle') }} s
left join {{ ref('partner_tier_history') }} h
    on s.partner_id = h.partner_id
   and s.submitted_at >= h.dbt_valid_from
   and (h.dbt_valid_to is null or s.submitted_at < h.dbt_valid_to)

wilson.description: Reusable score-bound algebra for a binomial proportion, with an explicit sampling-design caveat.

didMacro.description: Reusable two-period contrast; identification requires separate design checks.

diagnostics.title: Statistical diagnostics mart
diagnostics.description: Descriptive title, attempt, publication and snapshot-coverage diagnostics.
diagnostics.code:
-- Descriptive diagnostics only. Wilson bounds illustrate sampling uncertainty under
-- independent Bernoulli trials; these deterministic synthetic titles are not such a sample.
with title_scope as (
    select partner_id, first_pass_approved, published_regions, publication_lead_days
    from {{ ref('int_title_outcomes') }} where submission_attempts > 0
    union all
    select 'ALL', first_pass_approved, published_regions, publication_lead_days
    from {{ ref('int_title_outcomes') }} where submission_attempts > 0
), title_counts as (
    select partner_id, count(*) as titles_submitted,
        sum(first_pass_approved) as first_pass_approved_titles,
        sum(case when published_regions > 0 then 1 else 0 end) as titles_published
    from title_scope group by partner_id
), review_scope as (
    select partner_id, review_hours from {{ ref('int_submission_lifecycle') }}
    where review_hours is not null
    union all
    select 'ALL', review_hours from {{ ref('int_submission_lifecycle') }}
    where review_hours is not null
), review_stats as (
    select partner_id, count(*) as reviewed_attempts,
        round(avg(review_hours), 1) as mean_review_hours,
        round(quantile_cont(review_hours, 0.25), 1) as q1_review_hours,
        round(quantile_cont(review_hours, 0.50), 1) as median_review_hours,
        round(quantile_cont(review_hours, 0.75), 1) as q3_review_hours,
        round(quantile_cont(review_hours, 0.90), 1) as p90_review_hours
    from review_scope group by partner_id
), lead_stats as (
    select partner_id, count(*) as observed_publication_leads,
        round(avg(publication_lead_days), 1) as mean_lead_days,
        round(quantile_cont(publication_lead_days, 0.50), 1) as median_lead_days
    from title_scope where publication_lead_days is not null
    group by partner_id
), tier_scope as (
    select partner_id, tier_history_available
    from {{ ref('int_partner_tier_asof_submission') }}
    union all
    select 'ALL', tier_history_available
    from {{ ref('int_partner_tier_asof_submission') }}
), tier_stats as (
    select partner_id, count(*) as submission_events,
        sum(tier_history_available) as tier_history_covered_events
    from tier_scope group by partner_id
), rates as (
    select *, {{ safe_ratio('first_pass_approved_titles', 'titles_submitted') }} as approval_fraction
    from title_counts
)
select
    r.partner_id, r.titles_submitted, r.first_pass_approved_titles,
    round(100.0 * r.approval_fraction, 1) as first_pass_approval_pct,
    round(100.0 * {{ wilson_score_bound('r.approval_fraction', 'r.titles_submitted', 'lower') }}, 1) as wilson_lower_pct,
    round(100.0 * {{ wilson_score_bound('r.approval_fraction', 'r.titles_submitted', 'upper') }}, 1) as wilson_upper_pct,
    r.titles_published, r.titles_submitted - r.titles_published as titles_without_publication,
    v.reviewed_attempts, v.mean_review_hours, v.q1_review_hours,
    v.median_review_hours, v.q3_review_hours, v.p90_review_hours,
    l.observed_publication_leads, l.mean_lead_days, l.median_lead_days,
    h.submission_events, h.tier_history_covered_events
from rates r
left join review_stats v on r.partner_id = v.partner_id
left join lead_stats l on r.partner_id = l.partner_id
left join tier_stats h on r.partner_id = h.partner_id

didMart.title: Causal teaching model
didMart.description: A separate invented weekly cohort fixture calculates a DiD and pre-period placebo.
didMart.code:
-- A separate invented two-cohort teaching fixture, never an estimate from operational titles.
with period_means as (
    select cohort,
        case when week_number <= 4 then 'pre' else 'post' end as period,
        avg(first_pass_rate_pct) as mean_rate_pct
    from {{ ref('hypothetical_workflow_weeks') }}
    group by cohort, period
), means as (
    select
        max(case when cohort = 'treated' and period = 'pre' then mean_rate_pct end) as treated_pre_pct,
        max(case when cohort = 'treated' and period = 'post' then mean_rate_pct end) as treated_post_pct,
        max(case when cohort = 'comparison' and period = 'pre' then mean_rate_pct end) as comparison_pre_pct,
        max(case when cohort = 'comparison' and period = 'post' then mean_rate_pct end) as comparison_post_pct
    from period_means
), placebo_halves as (
    select cohort,
        case when week_number <= 2 then 'early' else 'late' end as half,
        avg(first_pass_rate_pct) as mean_rate_pct
    from {{ ref('hypothetical_workflow_weeks') }}
    where week_number <= 4
    group by cohort, half
), placebo as (
    select
        max(case when cohort = 'treated' and half = 'early' then mean_rate_pct end) as treated_early_pct,
        max(case when cohort = 'treated' and half = 'late' then mean_rate_pct end) as treated_late_pct,
        max(case when cohort = 'comparison' and half = 'early' then mean_rate_pct end) as comparison_early_pct,
        max(case when cohort = 'comparison' and half = 'late' then mean_rate_pct end) as comparison_late_pct
    from placebo_halves
), pretrend_slopes as (
    select cohort, regr_slope(first_pass_rate_pct, week_number) as slope_pp_per_week
    from {{ ref('hypothetical_workflow_weeks') }}
    where week_number <= 4
    group by cohort
), pretrend as (
    select
        max(case when cohort = 'treated' then slope_pp_per_week end) as treated_pre_slope,
        max(case when cohort = 'comparison' then slope_pp_per_week end) as comparison_pre_slope
    from pretrend_slopes
), time_gap as (
    select avg(case when week_number > 4 then week_number end)
         - avg(case when week_number <= 4 then week_number end) as pre_post_mean_week_gap
    from {{ ref('hypothetical_workflow_weeks') }}
    where cohort = 'treated'
), result as (
    select
        m.*,
        round({{ difference_in_differences('m.treated_pre_pct', 'm.treated_post_pct', 'm.comparison_pre_pct', 'm.comparison_post_pct') }}, 1) as did_pp,
        round({{ difference_in_differences('p.treated_early_pct', 'p.treated_late_pct', 'p.comparison_early_pct', 'p.comparison_late_pct') }}, 1) as pre_period_placebo_pp,
        round(t.treated_pre_slope - t.comparison_pre_slope, 1) as pretrend_slope_gap_pp_per_week,
        g.pre_post_mean_week_gap,
        round({{ difference_in_differences('m.treated_pre_pct', 'm.treated_post_pct', 'm.comparison_pre_pct', 'm.comparison_post_pct') }} - g.pre_post_mean_week_gap, 1) as effect_if_1pp_week_drift
    from means m cross join placebo p cross join pretrend t cross join time_gap g
)
select * from result

lifecycle.title: Submission lifecycle
lifecycle.description: Window ordering identifies each title's first attempt; the macro calculates review hours.
lifecycle.code:
select
    s.submission_id,
    s.title_id,
    t.partner_id,
    s.submitted_at,
    s.reviewed_at,
    s.status,
    s.build_version,
    row_number() over (
        partition by s.title_id
        order by s.submitted_at, s.submission_id
    ) as attempt_number,
    {{ review_hours('s.submitted_at', 's.reviewed_at') }} as review_hours
from {{ ref('stg_submissions') }} s
join {{ ref('stg_titles') }} t on s.title_id = t.title_id

title.title: One row per title
title.description: Submission and publication streams aggregate separately before joining, preventing fanout.
title.code:
with submissions as (
    select
        title_id,
        count(*) as submission_attempts,
        sum(case when reviewed_at is not null then 1 else 0 end) as reviewed_attempts,
        sum(coalesce(review_hours, 0)) as review_hours_total,
        min(submitted_at) as first_submitted_at,
        max(case when attempt_number = 1 and status = 'approved' then 1 else 0 end)
            as first_pass_approved,
        max(case when status = 'approved' then 1 else 0 end) as ever_approved
    from {{ ref('int_submission_lifecycle') }}
    group by title_id
), publications as (
    select
        title_id,
        count(distinct storefront_region) as published_regions,
        min(published_at) as first_published_at
    from {{ ref('stg_publications') }}
    group by title_id
)
select
    t.title_id,
    t.partner_id,
    t.planned_release_at,
    coalesce(s.submission_attempts, 0) as submission_attempts,
    coalesce(s.reviewed_attempts, 0) as reviewed_attempts,
    coalesce(s.review_hours_total, 0) as review_hours_total,
    coalesce(s.first_pass_approved, 0) as first_pass_approved,
    coalesce(s.ever_approved, 0) as ever_approved,
    coalesce(p.published_regions, 0) as published_regions,
    s.first_submitted_at,
    p.first_published_at,
    case when p.first_published_at is not null and s.first_submitted_at is not null
        then date_diff('day', s.first_submitted_at, p.first_published_at)
    end as publication_lead_days
from {{ ref('stg_titles') }} t
left join submissions s on t.title_id = s.title_id
left join publications p on t.title_id = p.title_id

fact.title: Submission fact
fact.description: A review-attempt grain for flexible downstream analysis.
fact.code:
select
    submission_id,
    title_id,
    partner_id,
    submitted_at,
    reviewed_at,
    status,
    build_version,
    attempt_number,
    review_hours
from {{ ref('int_submission_lifecycle') }}

dimension.title: Partner dimension
dimension.description: A partner key with business-friendly attributes.
dimension.code:
select partner_id, partner_name, region, partner_tier
from {{ ref('stg_partners') }}

mart.title: Partner publishing mart
mart.description: Curated partner-level measures, with explicit denominators.
mart.code:
select
    p.partner_id,
    p.partner_name,
    p.region,
    sum(case when o.submission_attempts > 0 then 1 else 0 end) as titles_submitted,
    sum(o.first_pass_approved) as first_pass_approved_titles,
    sum(case when o.published_regions > 0 then 1 else 0 end) as titles_published,
    sum(o.published_regions) as published_storefront_regions,
    sum(o.submission_attempts) as submission_attempts,
    sum(o.reviewed_attempts) as reviewed_attempts,
    sum(o.review_hours_total) as review_hours_total,
    round(100.0 * sum(o.first_pass_approved)
        / nullif(sum(case when o.submission_attempts > 0 then 1 else 0 end), 0), 1)
        as first_pass_approval_pct,
    round(sum(o.review_hours_total) / nullif(sum(o.reviewed_attempts), 0), 1)
        as avg_review_hours,
    round(avg(o.publication_lead_days), 1) as avg_publication_lead_days
from {{ ref('dim_partner') }} p
join {{ ref('int_title_outcomes') }} o on p.partner_id = o.partner_id
group by p.partner_id, p.partner_name, p.region

semantic.title: Metric contract
semantic.description: Versioned definitions and evidence requirements; a portfolio contract, not a deployed service.
semantic.code:
# Portfolio metric contract. This file documents business meaning; it is not
# presented as a deployed dbt Semantic Layer service.
version: 1
domain: synthetic_partner_publishing
owner: partner_analytics_portfolio
grain: partner_id
source_model: mart_partner_publishing
metrics:
  first_pass_approval_rate:
    label: First-pass approval rate
    expression: first_pass_approved_titles / titles_submitted
    display: percentage
    meaning: Share of submitted titles approved on their first review attempt.
    exclusions: Titles with no submission.
  average_review_hours:
    label: Average review hours
    expression: sum(review_hours_total) / sum(reviewed_attempts)
    display: hours
    meaning: Mean elapsed hours per reviewed submission attempt.
  published_titles:
    label: Published titles
    expression: titles_published
    display: count
    meaning: Distinct titles with at least one publication event.
policy:
  partner_scope: Bind row access to the caller's authorised partner IDs before querying.
evidence:
  - metric_version
  - source_freshness
  - dbt_test_status
  - source_to_mart_lineage

tests.title: Fanout assertion
tests.description: A singular dbt test fails if the one-row-per-title model changes its grain.
tests.code:
select
    (select count(*) from {{ ref('stg_titles') }}) as source_titles,
    (select count(*) from {{ ref('int_title_outcomes') }}) as outcome_titles
where source_titles <> outcome_titles

exposure.title: Dashboard exposure
exposure.description: The dbt exposure links a proposed partner dashboard to its upstream mart.
exposure.code:
version: 2

models:
  - name: mart_partner_statistical_diagnostics
    description: Descriptive partner and overall summaries; Wilson calculations are teaching examples, not intervals inferred from a random sample.
    columns:
      - name: partner_id
        data_tests: [unique, not_null]
      - name: titles_submitted
        data_tests: [not_null]
  - name: mart_workflow_did_demo
    description: Difference-in-differences arithmetic over a separate, entirely invented two-cohort weekly fixture.
    columns:
      - name: did_pp
        data_tests: [not_null]
      - name: pre_period_placebo_pp
        data_tests: [not_null]
  - name: dim_partner
    description: One row per partner; a synthetic current-state dimension.
    columns:
      - name: partner_id
        data_tests: [unique, not_null]
  - name: dim_title
    description: One row per game or content title.
    columns:
      - name: title_id
        data_tests: [unique, not_null]
      - name: partner_id
        data_tests:
          - not_null
          - relationships:
              arguments:
                to: ref('dim_partner')
                field: partner_id
  - name: fct_submission
    description: One row per publishing review attempt.
    columns:
      - name: submission_id
        data_tests: [unique, not_null]
      - name: title_id
        data_tests:
          - not_null
          - relationships:
              arguments:
                to: ref('dim_title')
                field: title_id
      - name: status
        data_tests:
          - accepted_values:
              arguments:
                values: ['approved', 'rejected', 'pending']
  - name: mart_partner_publishing
    description: Partner-level publishing health. All title outcomes are combined at title grain before this aggregation.
    columns:
      - name: partner_id
        data_tests: [unique, not_null]
      - name: first_pass_approval_pct
        description: Approved on attempt one divided by titles with at least one submission, multiplied by 100.
      - name: avg_review_hours
        description: Total review hours divided by reviewed attempts.
      - name: avg_publication_lead_days
        description: Average days from first submission to first publication among published titles.

exposures:
  - name: partner_release_health
    label: Partner release health (synthetic portfolio example)
    type: dashboard
    maturity: low
    description: A possible partner operations dashboard using the governed publishing mart; no PlayStation dashboard has been deployed.
    depends_on:
      - ref('mart_partner_publishing')
    owner:
      name: VIM portfolio example
      email: portfolio@example.invalid

ci.title: Build on every change
ci.description: GitHub Actions runs dbt build and checks generated site evidence.
ci.code:
name: Verify NEXUS partner analytics

on:
  push:
  pull_request:

jobs:
  dbt-reference:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'
      - name: Install dbt and DuckDB adapter
        run: python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
      - name: Build and test synthetic data product
        run: dbt build --profiles-dir .
      - name: Verify site evidence matches working code
        run: |
          python scripts/export_metrics.py --check
          python scripts/build_snippets.py --check
